name: browse_assets
description: Browse lightweight source-asset cards in the current project's media pool. Returns identity, duration in milliseconds, dimensions, folder, processing lifecycle, source access, concise transcript/generation/audio facts, and query match snippets. Query terms are whitespace-separated and every term must match at least one returned text fact. Transcript matches include exact transcriptRangesMs that can be passed to inspect_asset. Results use stable ordering and offset/limit continuation with nextOffset. Search coverage distinguishes a real zero match from transcript data that could not be searched. status is only the asset processing lifecycle; it does not say whether the current host can read the source. Transcript readiness is independent: transcript.readyForEditing=true means transcript, Script, and caption work is ready even when status=processing or sourceAccess.cloud=not-available. Never report such an asset as still transcribing, retry its transcription, or remove/skip it merely because source upload remains pending. sourceAccess.cloud describes only the ChatCut cloud copy and matters only when the next operation explicitly requires cloud media bytes. sourceAccess.desktopRegistered records that a Desktop import was registered, not that the file still exists on this computer. A Desktop-local source can be inspected and exported without cloud upload. This never returns pixels; call inspect_asset after choosing an ID.

folder.description: Exact media-pool folder path, case-insensitive, for example "Master/B-roll".

offset.description: Zero-based result offset (default 0). For continuation, pass nextOffset and keep the same query and filters.

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.

query.description: Search text facts: asset id/name, folder, type/status, concise generation/property facts, or transcript text. This does not search pixels or visual actions.
